caseno:
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 336 of 1991 (Dhaka).
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 1989 (Jessore).
lawyer:
Mansurul Hoque Chowdhury, Deputy Attorney-General with MA Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General Moshfiqur Rahman, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State. 
Shawkat Ali Khan with Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
State ------ Petitioner
Vs.
M A Wahab, Advocate ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque J: In this Miscellaneous Case opposite parry, Mr. MA Wahab, an Advocate of this Court, was directed by a Division Bench on 29-5-89 to show cause why his name should not be referred to the Bangladesh Bar Council for taking disciplinary action against him for committing the following misconduct:- 

 Mr. MA Wahab, the learned Advocate for the appellant-petitioners, taking advantage of his position as the President of the Bar Association of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Jessore Bench, Jessore, a former Additional Judge of this Court and an Ex-Deputy Attorney-General, has been visiting the learned Judges of this Bench at the rest house of the Roads and Highways, where the learned Judges reside almost on every Friday and gossips for hours together. This unwanted visits of the learned Advocate to the residence of the Judges was not liked by some of the learned Judges and he was requested earlier, not to do so by some of them. The conduct of the learned Advocate in frequently visiting the residence of the Judges of this Court, is against the canons of professional conduct and etiquette and it comes within the purview of professional misconduct, as the intent of the learned Advocate, was malafide and he appears to have obtained the ad-interim bail on 14-5-89 in Criminal Appeal No. 13 of 1989 and Criminal Appeal No. 94 of 1987, taking advantage of his close association and acquaintance with the learned Judge of the Vacation Bench. 

 2. Mr. MA Wahab, the learned Advocate for the appellant petitioners in the appeals, reportedly approached, the Assistant Bench Officer of this Court Mr. Md Abdul Hasib Khan on 22-5-89 at 10- 00 AM and asked him to remove the order-sheet dated 12-2-89 of Criminal Appeal No. 13 of 1989, by which, the earlier petition for bail of one of the appellant-petitioners was rejected by myself and by Mr. Justice Md Mozammel Hoque; as stated by the Assistant Bench Officer in his written report dated 23-5-89. This conduct of the learned Advocate attempting to tamper with the record of this Court through the Assistant Bench Officer is not only a professional misconduct but also a criminal misconduct", 

 3. Opposite party filed an affidavit as well as a supplementary affidavit to the above allegations brought against him. In the affidavit-in-opposition he denied the aforesaid allegations of misconduct regarding visiting the residence of the Judges in the week and with malafide motive and asking the Assistant Bench Officer to remove the order-sheet containing order dated 12-2-89 rejecting the earlier prayer for bail in Criminal Appeal No.B of 1989. But he admitted the allegation of serving notices and copies of the petition for bail on the Assistant Attorney-General Mr. SA Hasan. 

 "(i) As the Vacation Bench is meant for dealing with only the urgent matters, it is not understood how an application for bail in a pending Criminal Appeal previously rejected by the Division Bench, could be filed before the Vacation Bench presided by the Single Judge, such petition entertained an ad-interim bail granted in the facts and circumstance of the present case, as stated, above, specially when no ground was taken in the petition for bail and no emergency case was made out. We are of opinion that the Vacation Bench has no jurisdiction to grant ad-interim bail in a case of this nature." 

 11. Before parting with this case we like to reiterate the well-known dictum that Justice not only should be done but should also be seen to have been done. If any member of the legal profession hobnobs with any Judge and such a member appears in any case before that Judge, the party adverse to his client gets apprehensive about getting fair justice from that Judge. Even if the client of that member of the profession wins the case by the merit of the same his adversary cannot dissuade himself from his doubt about the fairness in the matter and thus his faith in the administration of justice is shaken. So, in the greater interest of justice always a safe distance is to be maintained between the Judges and members of the legal profession retaining good relations and respect for each other. 

 In the result, the Criminal Miscellaneous Case is disposed of with the above observations and the opposite party is exonerated from the charges brought against him.
